name: run_shell
description:
- **Purpose**: Execute a tightly-scoped shell command on the user's local machine. Hello-world v1: read-only inspection inside ~/Documents only.
- **Allowed executables**: ls, find, cat, head, tail, grep, wc, pwd. Anything else is refused.
- **Allowed paths**: must reference paths inside ~/Documents. Path traversal (`..`) is refused. The EmiAi repo path is denied even if it sits under home.
- **Refused outright**: pipes (`|`), redirects (`>`, `<`, `>>`), command chaining (`;`, `&&`, `||`), backticks, command substitution (`$(...)`), network executables (curl, wget, ssh, scp, nc), destructive commands (rm, mv, cp, dd, sudo, chmod, chown).
- **Limits**: 30s timeout, output capped at 4 KB.
- **Authority**: requires `approval_min_authority: 99` — only the user (master_room session, CLI session) can invoke. Inbound emails / SMS / external messages cannot trigger this through dayflow without explicit user authorization.
- **Arguments**:
  - `command` (str, required): the shell command to execute.
  - `reason` (str, required): one-line explanation of why this command. Becomes part of the audit log.

inputs.name: command
inputs.description: The shell command to execute. Single command only — no chaining or redirects.

inputs.name: reason
inputs.description: One-line explanation of intent. Recorded in the audit log.

outputs.description: Combined stdout/stderr (truncated to 4 KB) plus exit code.

arguments_prompt:
Arguments for run_shell:
- command (required): single shell command, e.g. `ls -la ~/Documents`. No pipes, no redirects, no chaining.
- reason (required): one-line intent.

Example:
{
  "command": "ls -la ~/Documents",
  "reason": "User asked for the file listing of their Documents folder."
}
